title: Feature Request: Support ed25519 encryption/decryption
description:
Hi @gaborcsardi,
[Github now recommends and defaults to ed25519 encryption when generating SSH keys](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/generating-a-new-ssh-key-and-adding-it-to-the-ssh-agent). 
Currently `secret` only supports rsa encryption. Are there plans to support ed25519 encryption and decryption?

title: Using a vault with other languages
description:
Thanks for creating this useful package. I recently had the need to read a secret from an R vault using python. I wanted to do this natively and started working through the code to do it, but I was stumped by the fact that the aes key is saved as a serialized R object rather than just the key value.

Would you be open to saving the key value rather than the object? Unfortunately, this would break existing vaults, but perhaps there could be some versioning information added (or that already exists) to keep both functioning. The upside is there could be native interactivity with other languages.

I would be happy to do this work myself if you are open to the change.

title: list users with access to secret
description: hello! I am hearing from my IT folks that it would be handy to have a function that accepts a secret name and returns users who it is shared with. I don't see that as a security issue, right? I looked at the code for list_users and I think it would be straightforward to take that approach. Do you mind if I make a PR at some point?

title: Throw a warning if users with identical fingerprint exist?
description:
I recently had a very stupid bug in one of my packages. I had a duplicated user in vault/users with two identical .pem files with different filenames (the username was misspelled in one).  

The result was that the user got "access denied" for the secret he wanted to access, despite the secret being correctly shared with him. Obviously this was my mistake, but it was pretty hard to debug. I think it would be cool if `secret:::lookup_user()` issued a warning (or threw an error?)  on duplicate key files in /users

title: get secret from package?
description:
I just create my first R package with `secret`. When I'm inside my package project I can run `secret::get_secret("apikey")` and I get my apikey. 

Once I'm outside my project, I tried the following:

```
library(MyPackage)
secret::get_secret("apikey")
Error in secret::get_secret("apikey") : secret ‘apikey’ does not exist
```

I can get it to work if i do this:

```
secret::get_secret("apikey", vault = file.path(system.file(package = "MyPackage"), "vault"))
```

Is there a better way? Can I do something like lazy loading the vault when I load my package?

Thanks for your great work!

title: Inconsistent keys from local vs. GitHub?
description:
## Setup

- Local SSH key pair (`id_rsa` and `id_rsa.pub`) generated via `ssh-keygen`, in Cygwin on Windows 10.
- SSH key uploaded to GitHub.
- `add_user('local', public_key = local_key(), vault = vaultPath)`
- `add_github_user(github_user)`

Edit: I should note that this key pair does work. I use it regularly to login to servers and commit codes on GitHub. 

## Problem

On the local machine, secret encrypted using the GitHub key could not be decrypted using `local_key()`. For example,

```r
add_secret('secret', 'secret', users = github_user)
get_secret('secret', key = local_key())
```

results in an error message `Access denied to secret ‘secret’`. Encrypting and decrypting using `local_key()` works as expected.

## What I Tried

I copied the JSON response from GitHub key-retrieval API call and fed it to `openssl::read_pubkey()`, the resulting md5 is identical to the return of 

```r
openssl::read_key('~/.ssh/id_rsa') %>% openssl::read_pubkey()
```

But the files `local.pem` and `github_user.pem` are not identical. Am I doing it wrong?


## Information

```
> packageVersion('secret')
[1] ‘1.0.0’
> packageVersion('openssl')
[1] ‘0.9.9’
> R.version$version.string
[1] "R version 3.4.3 (2017-11-30)"
```

title: How do we deal with orphaned secrets when deleting a user?
description:
Imagine a secret `foo` is shared with `alice`, and only with `alice`.

If you delete `alice`, this will leave an orphaned secret `foo` in the system.

There is no way to interact with this secret, because the key file no longer exists.

How should we deal with this?

Options:

1. Throw a warning when leaving orphaned secrets behind?
2. Throw a warning and don't delete the secret?
3. Delete the user *and* delete the secret?

In either case, we should:

* Expose a function to identify orphaned secrets

title: Add github PAT to Travis config to enable tests
description:
The tests for `add_github_user()` fails on Travis, because Travis makes anonymous requests to github. Since there is a rate limit on github for anonymous requests, the test sometimes pass and sometimes gets a 403 error.

The resolution to this is to add a github PAT to the Travis repo.

This is described at https://itsalocke.com/using-travis-make-sure-use-github-pat/
